main_text.head: DE CONIVNCTIONE CIVITATIS GRONINGÆ CVM VLTRAIECTINIS.

p.i: P[?]Rimam sub hoc nomine mentionem ejus in probatis & fidis literarum monumentis (nam de tabula Romana ætate ac fide cur dubitem, demonstratum à me alibi est) usurpatam invenio in instrumento quodam donationis, quod est in tabulino Ecclesiæ Ultrajectinæ, scripto & signato anno Christi M. XL : quo in instrumento HENRICVS III Imp. cognomento NIGER, filius Conradi II Saliqui, eidem Ecclesiæ tempore Bernoldi præsulis confert jus prædij, quod ipse in villa GRONINGA videbatur possidere. Qua de donatione pauca dicam, ut & antiquitatem & veritatem in hac re illustrem. Cum Normanni vastatores totius tractus maritimi Ultrajectum quoq; occupassent, sacraq; & profana illic diripuissent, cuncta ferro & flamma pessum dedissent, successoresq; Hungeri, qui manus vastatorum vix fugiens evaserat, Daventriæ domicilium ac sedem collocassent, tandem Baldericus è Comitib. Clivia prognatus, quintus post Hungerum episcopus, primum per se

page.notes: The woodcut initial is an ornamented capital D-shaped letter; its exact letter is uncertain, so it is given as P[?]. The first word reads as "Rimam" (from rimor, "to search"). The page's catchword "vivente" is printed at the right foot. Text is set in italic from the first line to the last. Page number 51 is printed top right. No running head is printed because the page opens a division.
